introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Given two vectors
$$\mathbf{a} = x\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}, \qquad \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}, \qquad x, y \in \mathbb{Z},$$
and that $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k}$.
incertitudes: Question 2 (iii) : « the plane that contains a and b » est lu comme le plan dirigé par les vecteurs a et b (vecteurs directeurs), seule lecture cohérente avec les parties (i) et (ii) qui préparent le produit vectoriel. Si a et b étaient lus comme des points, le plan serait 2x + 2y + z = 3, mais l'énoncé parle de vecteurs.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the values of the real constants, $x$ and $y$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand the vector product as a determinant:
$$\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ x & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & y & -1 \end{vmatrix}
= \big((-2)(-1) - (1)(y)\big)\mathbf{i} - \big((x)(-1) - (1)(1)\big)\mathbf{j} + \big(xy - (-2)(1)\big)\mathbf{k}$$
$$= (2 - y)\mathbf{i} + (x + 1)\mathbf{j} + (xy + 2)\mathbf{k}.$$
Equating with $\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k}$:
$$2 - y = 1 \Rightarrow y = 1, \qquad x + 1 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 3, \qquad xy + 2 = 5.$$
Check on the third component: $xy + 2 = 3\times 1 + 2 = 5$, which agrees.

$$\boxed{x = 3,\; y = 1}$$
So $\mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are linearly independent. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two non-zero vectors are linearly dependent exactly when one is a scalar multiple of the other, i.e. when $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$.

Here $\mathbf{a} = (3, -2, 1)$ and $\mathbf{b} = (1, 1, -1)$. Suppose $\lambda\mathbf{a} + \mu\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$. Then
$$3\lambda + \mu = 0,\qquad -2\lambda + \mu = 0,\qquad \lambda - \mu = 0.$$
Subtracting the first two equations gives $5\lambda = 0$, so $\lambda = 0$, and then $\mu = 0$. The only solution is $\lambda = \mu = 0$, so $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are linearly independent.

(Equivalently, $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k} \neq \mathbf{0}$, so the vectors are not parallel.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the Cartesian equation of the plane that contains $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ and passes through the point with position vector $\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plane is parallel to both $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ (they are independent, by part (ii), so they span its direction), hence its normal vector is
$$\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k}.$$
The plane has the form $x + 4y + 5z = d$. It passes through the point $(0, 1, 1)$ (position vector $\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$), so
$$d = 0 + 4(1) + 5(1) = 9.$$
$$\boxed{x + 4y + 5z = 9}$$
Check: $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 3 - 8 + 5 = 0$ and $\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 1 + 4 - 5 = 0$, so both vectors lie in the direction of the plane.
